entities.name: Domnall Ilchelgach
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Domnall mac Muirchertaig, known as Domnall Ilchelgach and Domnall mac Maic Ercae, was a High King of Ireland from 560 CE to 566 CE.

He rose to power following the death of his father, Fíanna, who was High King of Ireland. His reign is notable for its military campaigns against neighboring kingdoms, particularly the kingdom of Ulster.

Domnall's most significant achievement was his victory over the Uí Néill kingdom in 562 CE, which secured his position as High King of Ireland and extended his control over much of the island.

After his death, Domnall was succeeded by his son, Fáelán mac Domnaill.

Domnall's legacy is complex and multifaceted, reflecting both his military prowess and his diplomatic acumen.

As he once said, 'A king who does not have the support of the gods will never achieve greatness.'

This quote encapsulates Domnall's understanding of the importance of divine favor in securing a monarch's power and legitimacy.
